title: How many skyscrapers does each city have?
description: A bar chart gives the number of skyscrapers in different cities. Three bars are estimated, then three statements are tested by counting bars and by asking what the chart really counts.
teaching_notes: One idea: a chart answers only the question it counts. Watch for children who read building heights into a chart that counts the number of buildings.

video_script.why: The child can read bars and now counts bars above and below one bar.
video_script.substitution: Counting bars longer or shorter than Mumbai's answers the first two statements.
video_script.anchor: The book's bar chart of the number of skyscrapers in different cities, with the bars for New York, Tokyo, London and Mumbai
video_script.payoff_line: The chart counts buildings, so it cannot tell where the tallest one is.

final_answer.value: (a) estimates about 315 (300 to 330), 165 (155 to 180) and 28 (20 to 35) (b) (i) valid (ii) valid (iii) cannot be judged from the chart
final_answer.spoken: the chart counts buildings, so it cannot tell where the tallest one is

maths_rules: estimates: New York about 315, Tokyo about 165, London about 28; nearby values are accepted
Mumbai about 86; 12 bars are longer, so the first statement is valid
7 bars are shorter, so the second statement is valid
the chart counts buildings, not their heights, so the third cannot be judged
check: 315 > 165 > 86 > 28, so New York and Tokyo are among the 12 longer bars and London among the 7 shorter
video_script.design: One bar chart. Three bars are read off the line, then bars are counted either side of Mumbai's bar.
open_questions: The bar values (New York 315, Tokyo 165, London 28, Mumbai 86, neighbours Kuala Lumpur 154, Shanghai 183 and Moscow 46) and the counts 12 and 7 come from the worklist, because the chart is an image in the book and could not be checked.

beats.on_screen: To find: estimates for New York, Tokyo, London; are statements 1, 2 and 3 valid? 1: only 12 cities have more skyscrapers than Mumbai. 2: only 7 cities have fewer. 3: the tallest building in the world is in Hong Kong.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>It reaches about three hundred and fifteen. A reading from three hundred to three hundred and thirty is accepted.

beats.on_screen: Tokyo ≈ 165 (between Kuala Lumpur 154 and Shanghai 183); London ≈ 28 (below Moscow 46)

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, estimate Tokyo and London. The Tokyo bar lies between two bars.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Kuala Lumpur has one hundred and fifty four, and Shanghai has one hundred and eighty three. Tokyo is about one hundred and sixty five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The London bar is shorter than Moscow's forty six. It is about twenty eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, test the first statement. Count the bars longer than Mumbai's bar.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>There are twelve of them.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Only twelve cities have more skyscrapers than Mumbai, so the statement is valid.

beats.on_screen: statement 2: bars shorter than Mumbai's 86: 7 bars - valid

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, test the second statement. Count the bars shorter than Mumbai's bar. There are seven.
